Subject: Post-call recap — procurement routing, budget owners, next steps

Hi Sophie — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum: 

Summary from call
- Commercial path options discussed: AWS Marketplace (centralized billing) vs. direct PO (preferred for multi-year committed deals).
- Primary questions for procurement: do you need a Marketplace SKU subscription or a PO for initial purchase? Any legal redlines required up front?
- Budget/approval mapping: you mentioned Finance may own purchase approval but unsure who signs. We need: Economic buyer, Finance sponsor, and Contract signatory.

Actions I’ll take
- Send the procurement questionnaire (attached) for procurement to fill out.
- Draft SOW v1 for review and share DocuSign when we have routing preference.

Actions for Brightleaf
- Confirm preferred payment method (Marketplace subscription vs PO charged to central ledger).
- Share list of approvers: economic buyer, finance sponsor, and signatory with emails.

Attachments: procurement_questionnaire.xlsx (answers will speed contracting), SOW_v1_redwood.pdf (draft).

Proposed next meeting: 30 minutes with procurement + finance next week (Thu/Fri). Let me know which day works.

Thanks — Mateo

Thanks Mateo — helpful recap. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Marketplace vs PO: Our procurement group prefers AWS Marketplace for pilots and low-touch subscriptions, but for committed multi-year purchases they typically require a PO and internal purchase approval so spend hits the proper cost centers. We may need both: Marketplace for onboarding, PO for the committed contract.

2) Finance sponsor: Alex Chen (VP Finance) will sponsor the purchase from a budget perspective. I copied Alex and procurement on this thread to start the approvals path.

3) Signatory: final contract signatory is likely Amy Park (COO), but procurement will confirm required signatory level depending on T&Cs and spend.

Procurement, could you confirm expected lead times for PO issuance, any required vendor setup forms, and whether we can route an initial marketplace subscription while PO is processed?

I’ll try to get Alex to reply with budget cadence this week.

— Sophie
Sophie Martin
Head of Product Partnerships, Brightleaf Health

Hi procurement team — Mateo from Redwood here, looping per Sophie’s note. Quick ask: 

Could you confirm the following so we can route the right commercial path: 
- PO lead time (days from approval to PO issuance) and typical payment terms (Net 30/45/60).
- Whether Brightleaf requires a vendor setup packet or W-9 (we can supply immediately).
- If a temporary Marketplace subscription is acceptable while PO is processed.
- Any required contract addenda or insurance limits that will affect the SOW.

Attached: SOW_v1_redwood.pdf and procurement_questionnaire.xlsx (we filled preliminary fields — procurement answers will finalize routing).

If easier, happy to schedule a brief sync with Karthik (cc’d) to answer technical gating items.

Thanks — Mateo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap — procurement routing & budget owner mapping (internal)

Internal note — quick alignment and ask list before procurement responds: 

1) Discount/approval thresholds: If Brightleaf requests more than a 15% discount or a multi-year commitment with SLOs, we need Director approval (Ben). Anything >25% or enterprise credit terms needs VP signoff (Marissa).

2) Finance sponsor verification: Sophie indicated Alex Chen — can someone confirm Alex’s email and whether he owns the cloud budget or a pooled R&D budget? If pooled, we may need CFO/COO for sign-off.

3) Marketplace SKU mapping: Karthik, please prepare a one-pager mapping our product SKUs to Marketplace SKUs so procurement can validate billing flow. Aim to have this by EOD.

4) Contingency routing: propose we offer an initial 3-month Marketplace subscription (card) to get them running while PO is issued, then discount and convert to annual PO contract at renewal. Legal to confirm migration language.

Next steps: 
- Mateo: confirm Alex’s contact and proposed meeting times with procurement.
- Karthik: SKU mapping and short technical note on what needs to be in SOW to avoid infra/region blocks.
- Ben: ready to approve up to 15% discount if needed; escalate beyond.

Thanks — Marissa
